Category 4 - Biorational / Biopesticides.one: Registration of biopesticides for agriculture: microbials (4.1), consortia (4.1.2), botanicals (4.2) and pheromones (4.3).

pts: New microbial strain: 4.1 · strain already registered u/s 9(3): 4.1.1
Mixture of microbial strains: 4.1.2 consortium
Plant-based: 4.2, with special rules for eucalyptol, rotenone, cymbopogon, pyrethrum, PGRs, neem
Pheromones / semiochemicals: 4.3

4.1 Microbial pest control agents.one: Documents and data for registering microbial biopesticides: bacteria, fungi, NPV and GV.
nums: other contaminants per g or ml; pathogens such as Salmonella must be absent
sample for DNA fingerprinting (NBAIM) and for CIL verification
minimum POB per ml/g for NPV (GV: 5 × 10⁹ capsules)

pts: MOU / licence or authorisation from the strain's inventor (Annexure I)
Undertakings: free from chemical / botanical pesticides (II), composition (III), GMO-free (IV)
Form-I, BOD resolution, PAN, incorporation certificate
NBAIM fee receipt for DNA verification; strain deposited in the National Repository
Genus, species, strain, source of origin, specification, manufacturing process
Moisture, carrier and additive percentages, contaminant counts
Antagonists: dual culture must give at least 50% reduction (35% for bacteria)

watch: First-time strain not meant for field use: chemistry data is not required

4.1.1 Already registered formulation / s.one: Short route for a microbial product using a strain already registered u/s 9(3): one folder of documents.
nums: sample each to NBAIM (DNA fingerprint) and to CIB&RC (PRV)

pts: Form-I with fee, BOD resolution, PAN, incorporation certificate
Composition exactly as the earlier 9(3) registrant; approved label / leaflet
Inventor authorisation or undertaking (Annexure I); strain accession number
Undertakings: no chemical pesticides (II), composition (III), GMO-free (IV)
Original NBAIM fee receipt
Checked by the Chemistry division; no preliminary scrutiny
NBAIM reports directly to CIB&RC whether the DNA matches the original strain
Toxicology from non-GLP labs is accepted for biopesticides

watch: Declared shelf life (12 / 6 / 4 months) and IS 8190 packing are binding; violations can lead to prosecution

4.1.2 Consortium of biopesticides.one: Registering a mixture of compatible microbial strains (a consortium); same as single biopesticides except the points below.
nums: genome identity with a registered strain: no mother-culture data needed

pts: Only the formulated consortium needs data, not each mother culture (if already registered)
Give the ratio of each strain in the formulation
Strains should be compatible, broad-spectrum, with different modes of action
Inhalation for entomopathogenic bacteria; pulmonary for antagonists, fungi and virus
Cell culture and intravenous study for baculovirus
Only organisms on the list (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas, Bacillus, Beauveria, Metarhizium…); others need Schedule inclusion first

4.2 Botanical / plant origin pesticides.one: Data for plant-based pesticides: neem, eucalyptol, cymbopogon, pyrethrum, rotenone, essential oils.

pts: Home-made remedies for own use need no registration; anything sold does
Data waivers possible for well-studied substances, if justified
9(4): same plant part, same extraction process and identical composition as the 9(3) registrant
Plant part used, extract content, composition, BIS-format specification
Undertaking that no chemical pesticide is added; ATR from NABL / GLP lab
Shelf-life data not needed for eucalyptol, rotenone and cymbopogon products
Bio-effectiveness and phytotoxicity on target crops; waiting period, application details
Six acute studies for all; longer-term studies for 9(3) TI / TIM
9(4): no bio-efficacy or toxicity data
